headline: Budget committee weighs cuts, housing bonds; wastewater cut fails 4–4

meeting.body: Maui County Council Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee
meeting.voteItem: Add up to $40,000 to environmental protection grants for the Haʻikū Community Association stream testing program
meeting.summary: Testifiers urged Tutu and Me preschool funding; a motion to delete a village wastewater project's funding failed 4–4; domestic violence housing bonds passed.
meeting.recap: The committee continued its fiscal year 27 budget review.[[0:05:03]] Many testifiers asked the County to fund the Tutu and Me preschool after federal funds ended.[[0:08:32]] A co-director of the Maui Wildfire Exposure Study said more than 2,000 residents have taken part.[[0:15:14]] A testifier opposed proposed water rate hikes, including a $19.80 top tier.[[1:40:05]] The budget director said the mayor pledged up to $9.5 million for a village wastewater project.[[2:58:44]] A motion to delete that project's funding failed on a 4–4 vote.[[3:15:00]] The committee cut funding for Treasury positions on a 7–1 vote.[[3:32:13]] A fireworks fee increase was dropped because state law sets the $110 fee.[[4:19:22]] A council member proposed a $6 million Lahaina Community Land Trust grant.[[4:31:47]] A council member moved $4.5 million in bonds to buy homes to lease to domestic violence victims.[[4:36:44]] That motion passed with nine ayes.[[4:48:17]]
decided: The committee voted to reconsider the accounts program cut, and the mover withdrew the motion.
meeting.next: A proposed explosives permit fee increase was set aside while attorneys research it. A rental program funding request was set aside to revisit later.

issues.oneLine: A testifier opposed the proposed water rate increases.
issues.why: The testifier said neighbors got high bills when meters went unread for months and use landed in the top tier.
issues.brief: The testifier said the budget's top tier charges $19.80 per thousand gallons above 50,000 gallons.[[#1]] The committee passed up to $40,000 for a community association's stream testing program.[[#2]]
